crime.value: Murder of a blackmailer by gunshot at an isolated carriage house; central question: where is the body and who will control the knowledge of it?
crime.quote: I had also been able to hear the muffled report which had abruptly terminated their conversation.

victim.value: A small, slender blackmailer with sharp features exploiting Uncle Walter's affair with a blonde showgirl; killable because he escalated extortion demands.
victim.quote: a blackmailer—and not at all a clever or cautious one...the man really had been quite stupid to have accepted such terms

closed_world.value: A small rural estate with a carriage house, eucalyptus grove, and creek boundary; inhabited only by Uncle Walter, Harold, Aunt Pearl, and maid Elsie.
closed_world.quote: this small estate except for myself. Uncle Walter, and Aunt Pearl...Across the dry creek which formed the rear boundary line

culprit_and_motive.value: Uncle Walter shot the blackmailer to end escalating extortion; he is impulsive, tightfisted, and hiding an affair from his wife.
culprit_and_motive.quote: Uncle Walter was equally as stupid...He also apparently had a predilection for beautiful blonde show girls...blackmailed. He had committed murder

investigator.value: Harold, the eleven-year-old nephew who witnesses the murder from the oleander bushes and becomes the de facto investigator and manipulator of the crime's aftermath.
investigator.quote: I had gone for a short walk, and had noticed him sneaking out...had been able to hear every word...I found the body quite easily
